prompt: How many orders are waiting to be shipped?
golden: SELECT count(*) FROM app_core.orders WHERE status = 'placed'
note: Vague enum wording. Stored statuses are draft/placed/shipped/cancelled: drafts were never submitted and cancelled orders will not ship, so 'waiting to be shipped' is 'placed'. The schema sent to the model does not list the values.

prompt: Sum of total_cents over all orders with status Shipped
golden: SELECT sum(total_cents) FROM app_core.orders WHERE status = 'shipped'
note: Stored values are lowercase ('shipped'); a literal 'Shipped' matches nothing.

prompt: How many orders were placed on a Saturday or a Sunday?
golden: SELECT count(*) FROM app_core.orders WHERE extract(isodow FROM placed_at) IN (6, 7)
note: Day-of-week numbering trap: Postgres dow is 0=Sunday..6=Saturday, isodow is 1=Monday..7=Sunday.

prompt: How many orders have notes that do not mention manual review? Orders with no notes count too.
golden: SELECT count(*) FROM app_core.orders WHERE notes IS NULL OR notes NOT ILIKE '%manual review%'
note: NULL trap: NOT ILIKE drops the NULL-notes rows (it returns 0 here).

prompt: What percentage of customers were born before 1970? Round to 2 decimal places.
golden: SELECT round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE date_of_birth < DATE '1970-01-01') / count(*), 2) FROM app_core.customers
note: Integer-division trap: count/count in integer arithmetic gives 0 or 30 instead of 30.83.

prompt: Top 5 customers by item revenue (sum of quantity times unit_cents over the items of their orders), excluding cancelled orders. Show only the customer email and the revenue.
golden: SELECT c.email, sum(i.quantity * i.unit_cents) FROM app_core.customers c JOIN app_core.orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN app_core.order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' GROUP BY c.id, c.email ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 5
note: Three-table join + aggregate + filter. No ties in the top 5.

prompt: For each order status, the 3 SKUs with the highest item revenue (quantity times unit_cents) in orders of that status. Show status, sku and revenue.
golden: SELECT status, sku, revenue FROM (SELECT o.status, i.sku, sum(i.quantity * i.unit_cents) AS revenue, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY o.status ORDER BY sum(i.quantity * i.unit_cents) DESC) AS rn FROM app_core.orders o JOIN app_core.order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.status, i.sku) t WHERE rn <= 3
note: Top-N per group (window function). No ties at rank 3 in the seed, so row_number/rank agree.

prompt: Each customer's most recently placed order: customer id, order id and placed_at. Ignore orders that were never placed (placed_at is empty).
golden: SELECT DISTINCT ON (customer_id) customer_id, id, placed_at FROM app_core.orders WHERE placed_at IS NOT NULL ORDER BY customer_id, placed_at DESC
note: Greatest-per-group. Postgres sorts NULLs first under DESC, so forgetting the filter returns draft-only customers with a NULL row.

prompt: How many customers have never had an order with total_cents above 450000? Include customers with no orders at all.
golden: SELECT count(*) FROM app_core.customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM app_core.orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id AND o.total_cents > 450000)
note: Anti-join (83). The naive 'customers with an order <= 450000' gives 120.

note: Needs a subquery/join on customers in the WHERE; scope checked against golden rows (71 orders).
